extracted.intended_audience: current and aspiring science writers; students and instructors in science writing and journalism; scientists interested in science communication
extracted.subtask_description: A practical field guide for producing and evaluating science journalism across media, beats, and styles, covering craft, markets, ethics, and specialized subject areas. Useful for reporters, freelancers, editors, and scientists who communicate to public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Story Ideas and Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to discover compelling science story ideas and identify reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter devoted to techniques for sourcing stories and finding expert and documentary sources for science reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting from Science Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: How to read, interpret, and report on findings published in scientific journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers how to translate journal articles into accurate news stories for nonexpert audiences and how to vet claims in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and Using Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for understanding statistical claims and using statistics correctly in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice on interpreting statistical results, avoiding misrepresentation, and explaining uncertainty to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Well About Science: Techniques From Teachers of Science Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructional techniques from experienced teachers on writing clear, accurate, and engaging science prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes craft advice and pedagogical approaches to improve clarity and reader comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking Your Story to the Next Level
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice for elevating ordinary reporting into more impactful, in-depth, or memorable stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques for deeper reporting, narrative structure, and adding context or human interest to science stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding a Voice and a Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on developing an individual writing voice and appropriate stylistic choices for science writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses balancing personality with clarity and accuracy across different outlets and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cover science effectively for small, local newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market-specific advice on story selection, localizing science topics, and constraints of small newsroom resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches and expectations when writing science for major metropolitan or national newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers pitching, depth of coverage, and editorial standards at large outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular Magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write for general-interest magazines that cover science for broad audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on feature-length storytelling, narrative techniques, and tailoring content to magazine readerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade and Science Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for writing for trade publications and specialty science journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers differences in audience knowledge, tone, and technical depth appropriate to professional and scholarly publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast Science Journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and techniques for reporting science on radio and television.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers scripting, interview techniques, sound/visual storytelling, and constraints of broadcast formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelance Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical advice on working as a freelance science writer, including pitching and business practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers finding markets, negotiating contracts, managing multiple assignments, and sustaining a freelance career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Books
rubrics_metrics.description: How to research, structure, and write science books for various audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on long-form narrative, working with publishers, and planning book-length projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular Audiences on the Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for writing science content for general web audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers web formats, attention economy, hyperlinks, multimedia, and tailoring voice for online readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Audiences on the Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for writing web content targeted to readers with specific science interests or expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes community expectations, depth of explanation, and use of technical detail appropriate for niche online audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and practices of editing science content for accuracy, clarity, and audience fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers fact-checking, structural editing, line editing, and collaboration between writers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for producing accurate, clear science copy under tight time constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tips for rapid reporting, prioritizing facts, and avoiding common deadline pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for conducting in-depth investigative journalism in science-related topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers research techniques, document analysis, cultivating sources, and ethical/legal considerations for probes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gee Whiz Science Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: A style that emphasizes wonder and accessibility in presenting scientific discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses when and how to use upbeat, enthusiastic tones without sacrificing accuracy or skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for explaining complex scientific ideas clearly and accurately to lay readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques for breaking down concepts, using metaphors and analogies, and structuring explanations for comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Using narrative structures and storytelling techniques in science journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers character, scene-setting, pacing, and integrating scientific facts into compelling narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Science Essay
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and technique for essays that reflect on science, its meaning, and its societal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses voice, personal perspective, and balancing reflection with factual grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reporting on medical topics and health care issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers medical evidence, patient stories, clinical research interpretation, and ethical sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infectious Diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cover infectious disease reporting, including outbreaks and epidemiology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes interpreting surveillance data, sources in public health, and communicating risk and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches to reporting on nutrition science and dietary research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers evaluating studies, avoiding hype, and placing results in proper context for consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for reporting on mental health research and issues sensitively and accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses stigma, terminology, interpreting psychiatric research, and ethical reporting on vulnerable subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Biology of Behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on behavioral biology and neuroscience topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on interpreting behavioral studies, avoiding deterministic claims, and contextualizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Genetics
rubrics_metrics.description: How to report on human genetics, genomics, and related ethical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers complexity of genetic findings, probabilistic interpretation, and societal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Cloning and Stem Cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of cloning, stem cell research, and associated controversies and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for handling controversial science topics with accuracy and sensitivity to ethical debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology and Engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on applied science, engineering advances, and technology developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes understanding technical processes, industry context, and potential impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for covering astronomy, planetary science, and space exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers communicating scale, uncertainty, mission context, and translating technical material for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches to environmental reporting, ecosystems, and human–environment interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes framing complex ecological issues, policy context, and reporting on environmental risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing about natural history, wildlife, and ecological storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers observational writing, descriptive techniques, and conveying scientific knowledge about nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earth Sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of geology, geosciences, and earth-system topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on explaining earth processes, hazards, and research methods to nonexperts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on climate science, climate change, and related policy and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers interpreting models and data, communicating long-term risk, and policy/public discourse context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: How to report about risk, probabilities, and public perception of hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques for communicating risk clearly, avoiding alarmism, and explaining uncertainty and tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists and Public Information Officers: Similarities and Differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the roles, ethics, and intersections between journalists and institutional communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores differences in incentives, access to information, transparency, and trust between these professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on institutional communications and reporting on university-based science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers relations with university PR, research communications, and navigating academic structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Communications During Crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: How institutions communicate during crises and how journalists should cover such communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on evaluating institutional messaging, verifying claims, and reporting responsibly in crisis situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on science from or about government agencies and their communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers understanding agency processes, FOIA/document use, and interpreting official reports and statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofits
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle science communications involving nonprofit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes assessing motivations, funding sources, and credibility when nonprofits are sources or producers of science content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museums
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicating science in museum contexts and covering museum-based science outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on exhibit interpretation, public programming, and institutional perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate Public Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: How corporations handle science communications and how journalists should evaluate corporate messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers PR strategies, conflicts of interest, and skepticism when companies disseminate scientific claims.
